name: Cornhub

benchmark.title: Vimeo Watch
benchmark.observed: Video discovery navigation separates channels, categories, curated picks and on-demand access. Cornhub adapts the catalogue/channel/watch hierarchy with original non-explicit cinematic artwork and its own black/orange identity.

adaptation: Compact black/orange video portal: search, category navigation, four-column thumbnail rows, durations and studio metadata. Unrelated entertainment promotion; not labelled a scam. Native video, channel, saved and membership views. No explicit media or external adult site links.

name: Form & Field

benchmark.title: IKEA Malaysia desks and computer desks
benchmark.observed: Category groups lead to product lists and shopping decisions. Adapted into a workspace collection, product specifications, finish/quantity choices, bag and delivery review.

adaptation: Product-list structure: compact retail search/navigation, category chips, four-column products, prices, dimensions and delivery options. Ordinary retail interruption. Fictional products and brand. Original generated workspace-photography.png supplies eight product images, not copied from the benchmark. Per-product materials, dimensions, finish/quantity options and cart. No actual checkout.

name: Framekind

benchmark.title: Adobe Stock
benchmark.observed: Central asset search, content-type navigation, curated collections, library and pricing entry. Adapted as an original illustration catalogue with library, asset detail and licensing choices.

adaptation: Asset library structure: search band, filter rail, artwork results, asset identifiers and license routes. Ordinary creative subscription/asset promotion. Uses only locally owned original art. Purchase stops at review.

name: Tiny Arcade

benchmark.title: itch.io games
benchmark.observed: Search and tag discovery sit alongside independent game cards and detail pages. Adapted as six fictional game entries, a shelf, developer journal and one playable star-collection mechanic.

adaptation: Indie game directory: filter sidebar, compact grid, cover art, tags and playable game route. Normal game advertisement with a genuinely playable local browser mini-game. Six titles share a disclosed simple mini-game mechanic, not six full games.

name: SecureLane

benchmark.title: Norton product catalogue
benchmark.observed: Security product navigation distinguishes device security, privacy, plans and help. Only its product-information vocabulary informs the fictional overview. Norton is a legitimate vendor, not presented as a scam.

cases.title: FTC: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams
cases.pattern: Bogus computer warnings and urgent help prompts are used to obtain money or remote access. The prototype uses invented web-scan results leading toward support, with the flow ending before remote access.

adaptation: Security account console: product navigation, protection-status cards, device list and review/plan routes. Fictional status dashboard, invented alerts, alert details, support options and a final educational stop. No device scanning, phone calls or remote sessions.

name: Orbit Player

benchmark.title: mpv media player
benchmark.observed: A focused media-player product page with overview, features, installation and release information. Adapted into a fictional player overview, formats/features, release table and component choices.

cases.title: Proofpoint: An Update on Fake Updates
cases.pattern: Fake update pages redirect normal browsing into a software-update lure and installation pathway. The prototype changes that observed browser-update mechanism into a fictional player/codec update context; it does not claim the exact fictional player is a documented campaign.

adaptation: Player utility site: screenshot-style player preview, platform download route and release/documentation sections. Update landing, release notes, platform selection and preselected components; final install click explains the lure without creating a file.

name: AppHarbor

benchmark.title: 7-Zip official site
benchmark.observed: Software overview includes a feature list, platform/architecture-specific downloads, license information and release history. Adapted into richer fictional app cards and technical detail pages. The official 7-Zip site is not a scam.

cases.title: Microsoft Security: Counterfeit installers to system compromise
cases.pattern: Counterfeit software-download sites impersonate trusted suppliers and distribute malicious installers. The prototype illustrates the professional catalogue/download wrapper using fictional applications, never real malware.

adaptation: Conventional software directory: category rail and application/version/platform/download table, architecture choices and release notes. Six fictional apps, searchable catalogue, app screenshots, feature/specification pages, release history and download assistant choices. No executables generated.

name: Lucky Circle

benchmark.title: Microsoft Rewards overview
benchmark.observed: Reward catalogue themes include gift cards, member benefits and a discover/earn/redeem pathway. Used only as a reference for understandable reward organisation; legitimate Microsoft Rewards is not called a scam.

cases.title: FTC: Fake Prize, Sweepstakes, and Lottery Scams
cases.pattern: Unexpected prizes followed by requests for processing, handling or shipping fees are classic advance-fee scams.

adaptation: Rewards-account structure: balance, product reward catalogue, redemption steps and eligibility route. Three invented rewards, selection, preset recipient, release-fee summary and final explanation. No actual winner claim, payment or personal data collection.

name: Perk Basket

benchmark.title: Groupon
benchmark.observed: Searchable deal discovery uses category navigation and individual offer detail. Adapted as four fictional daily-life offers and a local voucher wallet. Groupon is a legitimate layout reference, not alleged to be a scam.

cases.title: FTC: Consumer Protection Data Spotlight June 2023
cases.pattern: Reward/gift messages can lead to small shipping-payment requests that expose card information.

cases.title: FTC: Inside a low-cost trial scam
cases.pattern: An inexpensive trial can lead to a much larger monthly subscription. Prototype combines a reward survey and low-cost subscription pattern; it is a composite, not an exact reproduction of one campaign.

adaptation: Voucher marketplace: category links, designed voucher faces, offer metadata and claim steps. Offer categories, detail, three preset preference questions, activation cost plus visible recurring condition, then educational stop. No contact or financial fields.

name: NorthPost

benchmark.title: DHL Malaysia Track & Trace
benchmark.observed: Tracking uses a shipment reference and leads into status/help information. Adapted as a fictional courier tracking form, journey timeline and delivery-options pathway. DHL is not called a scam.

cases.title: US Postal Inspection Service: Smishing Package Tracking Text Scams
cases.pattern: Unsolicited delivery messages and unrecognised links claim a shipment needs action. The prototype adapts that fake delivery-management pattern into an advertising interruption rather than claiming an exact SMS reproduction.

adaptation: Courier structure: shipment-reference form, tracking number, shipment details and event timeline. Official source text inspected; rendered DHL request failed HTTP2. Invented tracking number, delivery exception, preset address, delivery window, small reprocessing charge and final explanation. No real tracking lookup or financial fields.
